source: at TRACE, 8.0.0's BCKeyAndCertificateFactory.buildAndSavePrivateKeyAndX509Certificate logs `created new X509{}with SAN Domain Names{}and IPs{}` with BouncyCastle's toString of each leaf it generates: on the first TLS context and each time the subject alternative names grew (a new Host header or SNI name), not on a handshake that reuses the leaf.; socketConnectionTimeoutInMillis bounds the first handshake, whose certificate generation can take over the default 20 s on a loaded machine

steps.note: the first TLS connection: the CA loads and the first leaf

tcp.text:
GET /x509/a HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Connection: close

steps.note: the same names again: the leaf is reused, no entry

tcp.text:
GET /x509/a HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Connection: close

steps.note: the reused-leaf connection's `disconnected and closed socket` lands before the next request's entries (without the pause the oracle logged it after them)
a plain request whose Host is a new name grows the SAN set (no leaf yet)
the next handshake mints a leaf carrying the new name

tcp.text:
GET /x509/a HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Connection: close

steps.note: a new SNI name: a leaf carrying it

tcp.text:
GET /x509/a HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Connection: close

steps.note: back to localhost: the names are unchanged, the leaf is reused

tcp.text:
GET /x509/a HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Connection: close

steps.note: TRACE LOGS: one `created new X509` entry per leaf minted, before the DEBUG `using certificate authority` entry for it; the random parts of the certificate are masked
